preconditions.description: The number of knitting needles K is between 1 and 50000 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= x <= 999 and 1 <= y <= 999 and 1 <= z <= 999 for (x, y, z, _, _, _) in needles)
preconditions.description: Each coordinate in the input is an integer between 1 and 999 inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(len(needle) == 2 and len(needle[0]) == 3 and len(needle[1]) == 3 for needle in needles)
preconditions.description: Each needle is represented by exactly two distinct 3D coordinate triples.

preconditions.expression: all(needle[0] != needle[1] for needle in needles)
preconditions.description: The two triples in each needle are distinct.

preconditions.expression: all(needle != other_needle for i, needle in enumerate(needles) for other_needle in needles[i+1:])
preconditions.description: All needles are represented by distinct sets of triples.

postconditions.expression: true_closed_chain == (any(all(needles[i] == { (x1, y1, z1), (x2, y2, z2) } for i in range(k)) and all(needles[(i+1)%k] == { (x2, y2, z2), (x3, y3, z3) } for i in range(k)) and (x1, y1, z1) == (xk+1, yk+1, zk+1) for k in range(3, K+1) for (x1, y1, z1), (x2, y2, z2) in needles[0] for (x3, y3, z3), (x4, y4, z4) in needles[1] for (x5, y5, z5), (x6, y6, z6) in needles[2] for (xk+1, yk+1, zk+1) in [ (x1, y1, z1) ]))
postconditions.description: true_closed_chain is True if there exists a sequence of k >= 3 distinct needles forming a true closed chain, where each consecutive pair shares a common 3D coordinate, and the first and last coordinates match.

postconditions.expression: floor_closed_chain == (any(all(needles[i] == { (x1, y1, z1), (x2, y2, z2) } for i in range(k)) and all(needles[(i+1)%k] == { (x2, y2, z2), (x3, y3, z3) } for i in range(k)) and (x1, y1) == (xk+1, yk+1) and all({ (x1, y1), (x2, y2) } != { (xj, yj), (xj+1, yj+1) } for j in range(k)) for k in range(3, K+1) for (x1, y1, z1), (x2, y2, z2) in needles[0] for (x3, y3, z3), (x4, y4, z4) in needles[1] for (x5, y5, z5), (x6, y6, z6) in needles[2] for (xk+1, yk+1, zk+1) in [ (x1, y1, zk+1) ]))
postconditions.description: floor_closed_chain is True if there exists a sequence of k >= 3 distinct needles forming a floor closed chain, where each consecutive pair shares a common 2D coordinate (ignoring z), the first and last 2D coordinates match, and all needle shadows are distinct.

postconditions.expression: stdout == (('True closed chains' if true_closed_chain else 'No true closed chains') + '\n' + ('Floor closed chains' if floor_closed_chain else 'No floor closed chains'))
postconditions.description: The output is two lines: the first line indicates whether a true closed chain exists, and the second line indicates whether a floor closed chain exists.
